items.title: Formal retail credit access doubles over past decade
items.summary: India’s formal retail credit market has expanded sharply over the past decade, with credit access rising from 35% of consumers in 2017 to 74% in 2026, according to TransUnion CIBIL. Consumption-led loans such as personal loans, credit cards and consumer durable loans have driven growth, shifting borrowing from asset purchases to lifestyle spending.

items.title: Indian Oil to hire dedicated vessel to ferry LPG cylinders from Sri Vijaya Puram to all islands
items.summary: Indian Oil Corporation Limited plans a dedicated vessel for LPG supply. This initiative aims to ensure uninterrupted cylinder delivery across remote islands. A five-year contract for transportation is now being sought. The estimated value of this tender stands at Rs 58.90 crore. This will significantly improve essential commodity supply chains in the Union Territory.

items.title: Sensex today | Stock Market Live: Sensex tops 78,150, Nifty above 24,390 as AI-fuelled global rally boosts sentiment
items.summary: Sensex, Nifty, Stock Price Live Updates: Indian benchmark indices extended gains on Thursday, supported by a Wall Street-led technology rally, strong foreign investor inflows and easing crude oil prices. Positive Asian markets and favourable derivatives positioning reinforced sentiment, keeping the Nifty comfortably above 24,400 despite lingering geopolitical risks.

items.title: Amazon, Flipkart slash fees as battle for smaller cities intensifies
items.summary: E-commerce giants Amazon and Flipkart are cutting seller fees to expand into smaller Indian cities. This strategy aims to attract more sellers and offer affordable products to consumers. Lower commissions reduce operating costs for merchants, enabling competitive pricing for buyers. Online shopping is rapidly growing in tier two and smaller markets across India. This shift focuses on capturing new customers from non-metro regions for future growth.

items.title: IndiGo's next chapter: Rahul Bhatia backs Willie Walsh to lead expansion
items.summary: IndiGo Managing Director Rahul Bhatia said incoming CEO Willie Walsh is motivated to make a lasting impact at the airline and will be instrumental in its international expansion. Walsh, who takes charge on August 3 after stepping down as IATA chief, brings experience across low-cost and full-service airlines as IndiGo enters its next phase of global growth.

items.title: Lupin launches generic Sugammadex injection in US
items.summary: Lupin Limited announced the launch of its Sugammadex Injection in the United States. This follows approval from the US Food and Drug Administration for its abbreviated new drug application. The company's injection is claimed to be bioequivalent to Merck's Bridion Injection. It is indicated for reversing neuromuscular blockade in adult and pediatric surgical patients. The launch occurred on Friday, as per a regulatory filing.

items.title: Who gets faster Internet? India's net world may soon have first class and economy
items.summary: India is reviewing its net neutrality rules to allow 5G network slicing, a move that could let telecom operators offer premium connectivity with guaranteed speed, latency and reliability. The policy shift could transform industries from healthcare to manufacturing while raising concerns about a two-tier internet where businesses and consumers pay for faster network performance.

items.title: Sainsbury's agrees to sell Argos for £120m
items.summary: Under the terms of the deal, Argos will still operate in Sainsbury's shops, sell Habitat products, and offer Nectar points.

items.title: Global Market: Euro zone, US bond yields log biggest monthly rise since March on Middle East inflation concerns
items.summary: Euro zone and US bond yields recorded their largest monthly increase since March as Middle East conflict concerns renewed inflation fears. Traders pushed back interest rate cut expectations, with Germany’s 10-year yield rising 28 basis points in July and US 10-year Treasury yields advancing 22.5 basis points despite a Friday dip.

items.title: Juniper Green Energy IPO Day 2: Issue subscribed over 40% so far, GMP slips. Should investors subscribe or stay away?
items.summary: Juniper Green Energy’s Rs 1,800 crore IPO received a muted response on the second day of bidding. The IPO’s grey market premium has also declined to around 2.67% from nearly 8% earlier, signalling expectations of limited listing gains.

items.title: Why high-conviction investor Cathie Wood bought Nvidia after it erased billions from May high
items.summary: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest bought nearly 78,965 shares of Nvidia across its five largest ETFs, worth around $15.5 million, after the AI chipmaker’s recent decline. The purchase reflects renewed confidence in Nvidia’s long-term AI growth prospects, despite the stock falling over 6% in the past five sessions and about 17% from its mid-May peak.

items.title: If India wants to compete with the world, it has to have one or two large airlines: IndiGo’s Rahul Bhatia
items.summary: IndiGo MD Rahul Bhatia defended the airline’s 66% domestic market share, saying 34% of its capacity operates on routes where no rival flies. He said scale is essential for India to build global aviation champions and dismissed criticism of IndiGo’s service as “noise”.

items.summary: Decision to market assets comes after talks with Ithaca Energy

items.summary: Commonwealth Bank of Australia said in a note on Friday that stronger oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz had eased market concerns after U.S.-Iran strikes earlier this week.

items.title: Global Market: Sony Q1 profit jumps 32%, earthquake impact yet to be assessed
items.summary: Sony Group reported a 32% year-on-year rise in first-quarter profit, driven by strong performances in its music, gaming and imaging businesses. However, the company warned it is still assessing the financial impact of the Kumamoto earthquake, which disrupted production at one semiconductor facility.

items.title: Explained: Why Kospi skyrocketed 18% today after massive selloff and what’s ahead for South Korea’s 'bipolar' stock market
items.summary: South Korea’s Kospi jumped 18% on Friday as US tech earnings triggered a 28% surge in Samsung and SK Hynix. The sharp rebound follows a 40% crash driven by single-stock leveraged ETFs, drawing retail protests. Nomura targets 10,000-11,000 for Kospi, while Citi downgraded the market to neutral over volatility.

items.title: IndiGo to decide on next aircraft order in 2030 after assessing new-generation planes: Rahul Bhatia
items.summary: IndiGo plans to wait until the early 2030s before placing its next aircraft order as it evaluates next-generation aircraft technologies that promise lower costs and emissions. Managing Director Rahul Bhatia said the airline is well positioned until 2035 with more than 900 aircraft on order, while focusing on sustainability, long-haul expansion and maintaining its cost advantage.

items.title: MTAR Tech shares hit 5% upper circuit again. What’s behind the renewed optimism?
items.summary: MTAR Technologies shares hit the 5% upper circuit for the second straight session after the company reported a strong Q1 performance, with net profit rising 364.5% year-on-year and revenue more than doubling. The aerospace and precision engineering company also raised growth visibility with an 80% FY27 revenue growth guidance, a Rs 504 crore nuclear order win and an expanded customer order worth around Rs 3,100 crore.

items.title: New insurance norms for hospital admission: 'Unnecessary hospitalisation' won't be allowed; doctors fear genuine mediclaims may be denied
items.summary: New insurance norms for hospital admission issued by the General Insurance Council advise that patients with uncomplicated fever be treated on an outpatient basis rather than admitted. While the council calls it advisory, doctors and nursing home owners fear insurers will use the guidelines to deny legitimate cashless claims, particularly at smaller hospitals.

items.summary: Mukul Mahavir Agrawal held 39,00,000 shares, equivalent to 1.12% of the total voting rights, of LT Foods by the end of the June quarter. LT Foods share price has given a multibagger return of over 125% in the last three years.

items.summary: The Road ministry said E20 petrol might hit your mileage by 2-6%, based on a study by ARAI, SIAM, and Indian Oil Corporation. The statement sparked a buzz because just a few days earlier, Petroleum ministry had given a different figure.

items.title: FIIs cut stakes in 72% of Nifty50 stocks, DIIs buy 82%. Here’s where the money moved
items.summary: India’s largest stocks are witnessing a major ownership shift as domestic institutions fill the gap left by foreign investors. FIIs cut stakes in 36 Nifty 50 companies, while DIIs raised holdings in 41, taking their index ownership to a record 25.9%. Max Healthcare saw the sharpest change, with FII holdings falling 13 percentage points and DII stake rising 12.5 points.

items.title: Air India, SkyDrive, Suzuki sign pact to study eVTOL aircraft use for medical logistics
items.summary: Air India, SkyDrive, and Suzuki will study eVTOL aircraft for medical logistics. This collaboration aims to address severe traffic congestion in India's major cities. The companies will combine their expertise to develop emergency medical transport solutions. This initiative seeks to improve India's medical infrastructure and reduce critical transit times.

items.title: M3M India to invest Rs 600 cr to build commercial project in Gurugram
items.summary: Realty firm M3M India will invest Rs 600 crore for a new commercial project. This project, named M3M Capital Financial Center, will span 1.42 acres. It will feature premium office spaces, multiplex units, and retail units for sale. The Gurugram-based company expects project completion by the year 2029. M3M Group plans further expansion through land acquisition and construction investments.
